set system host-name [parameter1].explanation: Configure the host name of the device.

parameters.name: hostname
parameters.explanation: The host name of the equipment is used to identify the equipment in the network.

parameters.name: lsr-id
parameters.explanation: The LSR ID in MPLS is used to identify devices within an MPLS network.

set protocols mpls label-protocol [param.explanation: Configures the tag distribution protocol for MPLS as LDP.

parameters.name: protocol
parameters.explanation: Label distribution protocols, such as ldp.

set protocols ospf area [parameter1].explanation: This command configures an OSPF area in Junos OS, where `[parameter1]` specifies the area ID, enabling OSPF routing within the defined area.

parameters.name: area
parameters.explanation: OSPF area ID.

network [parameter2]/[parameter3].explanation: Configure the network within the OSPF area.

parameters.name: network
parameters.explanation: Web address.

parameters.name: subnet-mask
parameters.explanation: bits of subnet mask.

parameters.name: interface
parameters.explanation: Interface name, e.g., g-1/0/0.

unit [parameter2].explanation: Configure the unit number of the interface.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.explanation: Interface unit numbers that distinguish between multiple logical configurations under the same interface.

family inet address [parameter3]/[parame.explanation: Configure IPv4 addresses for interfaces and subnet masks.

parameters.name: ip-address
parameters.explanation: The IPv4 address assigned to the interface.

parameters.name: subnet-mask
parameters.explanation: Bits of IPv4 subnet mask.

mpls traffic-eng tunnels.explanation: The command `mpls traffic-eng tunnels` enables MPLS Traffic Engineering (TE) on a Junos device, allowing the creation and management of TE tunnels for optimized traffic routing.

family inet policy input [parameter3].explanation: The command `family inet policy input [parameter3]` applies a specified firewall filter (`[parameter3]`) to incoming IPv4 traffic on an interface.

parameters.name: policy
parameters.explanation: Enter the policy name.

set firewall family inet filter [paramet.command: set firewall family inet filter pe
set firewall family inet filter [paramet.explanation: This command fragment configures an IPv4 firewall filter named `[parameter1]` in Junos OS, defining rules to control traffic based on specified conditions.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.explanation: Firewall filter name.

term [parameter2].explanation: This command fragment creates a term within an IPv4 firewall filter, where `[parameter1]` is the filter name and `[parameter2]` is the term name.

parameters.name: term
parameters.explanation: Filter term name.

from protocol [parameter3].explanation: The command fragment `from protocol [parameter3]` specifies a match condition in a Junos policy or filter, targeting traffic originating from the specified routing protocol.

parameters.name: protocol
parameters.explanation: The protocol type to be matched.

then [parameter3].explanation: Configure firewall filter terminologies and accept all traffic.

parameters.name: action
parameters.explanation: Action, accept indicates acceptance of traffic.

set class-of-service classifiers traffic.command: set class-of-service classifiers traffic match-all pe

parameters.name: classifier-type
parameters.explanation: Classifier type, for example, traffic.

parameters.name: classifier-name
parameters.explanation: Classifier name.

set class-of-service schedulers [paramet.explanation: The command `set class-of-service schedulers [parameter1]` configures a scheduler for traffic classes, defining parameters like bandwidth, priority, and buffer management for QoS.

parameters.name: scheduler-name
parameters.explanation: Scheduler name.

scheduler-weight [parameter2].explanation: The `scheduler-weight [parameter2]` command in Junos assigns a weight to a scheduler, influencing the bandwidth allocation for traffic classes in a hierarchical scheduling structure.

parameters.name: scheduler-weight
parameters.explanation: The weight value of the scheduler.

weight [parameter3].explanation: The `weight [parameter3]` command in Junos assigns a weight value to a route, influencing its preference in the routing table for load balancing or traffic engineering.

parameters.name: weight
parameters.explanation: Weight value.

set class-of-service policer [parameter1.explanation: The command sets a Class of Service (CoS) policer named `[parameter1]` to enforce traffic rate limits and apply actions like dropping or marking packets.

parameters.name: policer-name
parameters.explanation: Traffic policer name.

cir [parameter2].explanation: The command `cir [parameter2]` in Junos sets the Committed Information Rate (CIR) to the specified value in bits per second for traffic policing or shaping.

parameters.name: cir
parameters.explanation: Committed Information Rate, unit is pps (packets per second).

pps.explanation: The `pps` command in Junos measures the packet processing rate in packets per second, typically used for monitoring or troubleshooting network performance.

pir [parameter2].explanation: The command `pir [parameter2]` in Junos sets the Peak Information Rate (PIR) for a traffic policer, defining the maximum allowed traffic rate in bits per second.

parameters.name: pir
parameters.explanation: Peak Information Rate, measured in packets per second (pps).

pps.explanation: The command `pps` in Junos stands for "packets per second," used to specify the rate of packet transmission or processing in traffic policing or shaping configurations.

conform-action [parameter2].explanation: The `conform-action` command in Junos specifies the action to take when traffic conforms to a defined rate limit, with `[parameter2]` defining the specific action (e.g., `transmit` or `accept`).

parameters.name: conform-action
parameters.explanation: "Action to be taken when the rate is met."

exceed-action [parameter3].explanation: The `exceed-action [parameter3]` command in Junos specifies the action to take when traffic exceeds a defined rate, with `[parameter3]` defining the specific action (e.g., discard, mark, or policer).

parameters.name: exceed-action
parameters.explanation: Action when the rate is exceeded.

violate-action [parameter4].explanation: The `violate-action [parameter4]` command in Junos specifies the action (e.g., discard, mark, or log) to take when traffic exceeds a defined rate limit or policy.

parameters.name: violate-action
parameters.explanation: Action to be taken when the rate is violated.
